sample_unit: not reported (5 watermarking schemes across 11 LLMs and 7 VLMs on medical tasks)

links.outcome: Effect of watermarking (content provenance) on medical reasoning quality, terminology, hallucinations
links.effect: Watermarking can induce substantial degradation across failure modes, including lexical corruption, hallucinated terminology, and amplified misattribution or omission of image findings.
links.quote: Our results reveal that watermarking can induce substantial degradation across multiple failure modes, including lexical corruption, hallucinated terminology, and amplified misattribution or omission of image findings.

links.outcome: Whether general aggregate benchmarks mask clinically consequential failures without domain-specific evaluation
links.effect: Absence of domain-specific analyses plus aggregate metrics systematically obscures watermark-induced degradations in clinical text; domain-specific evaluation is called a prerequisite for safe deployment.
links.quote: Notably, we find that the absence of domain-specific analyses, combined with aggregate metrics that miss failures inherent to clinical text, can systematically obscure practical watermark-induced degradations.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating the impact of output watermarking on medical LLM/VLM quality using a human-expert-validated audit pipeline

screen.reason: Empirically tests the safety and performance impact of applying watermarking schemes (a provenance/traceability safeguard) to LLMs and VLMs across clinical reasoning benchmarks.
